subject: ArborTech MSA + Order Form: scope, data residency & IP carveouts
messages:
From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@arbortech.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Matt Glenn <matt.glenn@arbortech.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ArborTech MSA + Order Form: scope & residency questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. ArborTech is moving forward with a pilot that will embed Redwood Inference for our customer search augmentation feature. Before we get to signature, legal/procurement have two specific asks we want to surface now so we can avoid late-stage redlines:

- Data residency: we have EU customers in the pilot and need to confirm options for EU-only data residency for EU customer traffic. Can you confirm hosting regions and whether we can lock residency per-customer on the Order Form?
- IP carveouts: our legal team typically asks for an explicit carveout for customer-provided data and any customer-trained models or derivative models. We want to avoid assignment claims.

I've attached a party sheet and an initial list of technical questions (see ArborTech_PartySheet.xlsx). Procurement would also like an estimated timeline for contract review — target is to have an executed MSA + Order Form by July 15 to meet our internal release.

Could you confirm next steps and what info we should prepare for your side (e.g., SOC 2 copy, hosting region details, retention windows)?

Thanks,
Elena Ramos
Sr. Procurement Manager
ArborTech

--
Attachment: ArborTech_PartySheet.xlsx (spreadsheet, 45KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@arbortech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ArborTech MSA + Order Form: scope & residency questions

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the party sheet. Looping in Marissa (commercial contracting) and Jonas (security/compliance) so we can triage the asks.

Short answers up front:
- Data residency: we support region-scoped deployment and can specify EU-only routing on the Order Form for relevant customer traffic. We'll include residency as a checkbox in the Order Form and document it in Exhibit B.
- IP carveouts: Redwood's standard MSA includes a customer data carveout; we typically avoid assignments of derivative models but can propose language that explicitly preserves customer rights over customer-provided data and customer-trained artifacts. We'll propose a limited carveout for models trained on customer private datasets.

Next steps from our side:
1) Marissa will prepare an initial Order Form + Exhibit A (scope) and a redline-ready MSA with suggested carveout language.
2) Jonas will attach SOC 2 and provide recommended log retention defaults and hosting regions.
3) I'll propose a 30-min intake sync to walk the team through the draft.

We plan to send the first redline packet by EOD Thursday (Jun 26). Would ArborTech be available for a quick sync on Thu 6/26 at 11:00 AM PT?

Thanks — we'll include the artifacts in a single packet so procurement/legal has everything to review.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0129

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@arbortech.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft packet: Order Form v0 + Exhibit A (scope) + proposed carveouts

Hi Elena — attaching a first-pass packet for ArborTech (attached: OrderForm_v0.xlsx, ExhibitA_Scope_draft.docx). Key items called out below so legal can triage quickly:

1) Order Form / Residency options
- Field on Order Form: "Data Residency: US | EU | Global" — if EU selected, we will route inference requests originating from EU customers to EU-only capacity. Residency can be locked for the initial term and extended at renewal.

2) Exhibit A (scope):
- Pilot scope defined (search augmentation), QPS and expected peak tokens per request are noted. Please confirm the number of pilot seats and estimated 90-day token volumes.

3) IP / model carveouts (proposed language)
- Proposed paragraph: "Customer Data and Customer Models: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data. Any models or model artifacts trained exclusively on Customer Data shall be owned by Customer; Redwood shall have a limited license to perform inference for the Customer's benefit only."
- We flagged a potential compromise if ArborTech prefers a joint-license approach for derivative models — we can present both options to legal.

4) Logs & retention
- Default: access logs and request metadata retained for 90 days; aggregated telemetry retained longer for performance improvements. If ArborTech requires shorter retention we can discuss a custom retention term in the Order Form (noted under Exhibit D).

5) Attachments & evidence requested
- Please send SOC 2 contact or we will send Redwood's SOC 2 report and ISO summary.

Action items / ask from you:
- Confirm pilot seats and token volume estimate (cell B12 in OrderForm_v0.xlsx).
- Indicate preferred residency option (US/EU/Global).
- Confirm whether the proposed IP carveout language meets ArborTech's baseline.

If that looks OK, let's meet Thu 6/26 at 11:00 AM PT to walk the packet and capture redline priorities.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Commercial Counsel | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

--
Attachments: OrderForm_v0.xlsx (sheet with pricing/fields), ExhibitA_Scope_draft.docx (Word doc)

From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@arbortech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Matt Glenn <matt.glenn@arbortech.com>, ArborTech Legal <legal@arbortech.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Jun 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft packet: Order Form v0 + Exhibit A (scope) + proposed carveouts

Marissa / Kimberly — this is very helpful, thank you. A few quick clarifications from Legal before the sync: 

- IP carveout: the proposed language is a good start, but our legal team will push for an explicit "no assignment" clause for derivative models where ArborTech provides the training dataset. They want the phrase "Customer shall retain all rights in Customer Data and Customer-Trained Models". If Redwood prefers the license approach, please include the alternate wording in the redline packet so we can compare.
- Logs retention: we need assurance that request payloads (even if encrypted) are not retained beyond 90 days. Can Redwood confirm you can enforce a 90-day deletion for request payloads tied to EU residency?
- Timeline: July 15 execution is preferred. Procurement will review the packet on Friday and provide first-pass comments.

We confirm the 11:00 AM PT sync Thu 6/26. I'll have our legal counsel on the call.

Best,
Elena Ramos
Sr. Procurement Manager
ArborTech
